title: Independent Comparator replay + human statement-fidelity review of the ~20 configs behind the opportunity matrix
summary: The library has zero sorry/admit/native_decide/extern/custom axioms in 26M lines, and all 416 configs allow only the three standard axioms. However, no Comparator run or attestation is published, and formalization.yaml says review: unchecked (agent-written statements). Replaying Comparator with nanoda in the documented sandbox, plus a domain-expert sign-off on each challenge file, turns the confidence column from claimed into verified.

targets.name: HarmonicArtin challenge (needs expert check of Salvetti encoding)

beneficiaries: Everyone citing the drop: this study's opportunity matrix, formal-conjectures, erdosproblems.com, practitioners who want to cite 131/179/276/325 as theorems
first_step: On a machine that can reach the Mathlib cache, run lake update && lake exe cache get, then comparator on ComparatorChallenges/CirculantHadamard.json (9.8k-line closure) to validate the pipeline, then the rest of the list. Use nanoda as an external kernel.
measurement: Per-config pass/fail log, #print axioms output, hashes, plus a signed reviewer note per challenge file (statement matches paper: yes/no/caveat).
risks: The fresh build may break: 23 dependency patches are applied by Lake hooks. 003 (556k lines + patched PNT+) and 266 (2.8M lines) closures are heavy and need high vm.max_map_count. A reviewer may find a mis-stated predicate, which is a useful outcome.

title: Bridge OAI theorems to independently written formal-conjectures statements (30 FC files already link openai/math proofs)
summary: formal-conjectures holds 36 formal_proof links to openai/math, attached to statements written independently with sorry (e.g. circulant Hadamard via Hadamard.IsHadamard' and Matrix.circulant; Erdos 970 via jacobsthalFunction). A short Lean bridge deriving each FC statement from the OAI theorem leaves only a small, human-checkable bridge as the fidelity risk, and lets FC drop sorry on 'research solved' entries.

beneficiaries: formal-conjectures maintainers, erdosproblems.com (which plans to link checkable Lean), anyone needing a statement with two independent authors

measurement: Number of FC 'research solved' entries whose sorry is replaced by a compiled bridge.
risks: Toolchain/Mathlib version skew between FC HEAD and the OAI pin (v4.34.1, Mathlib d13f23b) may require extracting OAI closures. FC policy may prefer not to depend on a 1.5 GB external library.

title: Metadata/hygiene PRs to openai/math: index 227 missing configs, flag support-only results, fix stale links, remove challenge axiom
summary: formalization.yaml lists 189 of 416 configs; the other 227 configs (106 families, including 131, 374, 266, 149, 012, 187, 317) are missing. It does not distinguish the 14 support-only docs. Docs 342 and 376 link pre-repair manuscripts, and HarmonicGrowth's challenge proves main from 'axiom mainStatement'. Fifteen required packages (11 lana-agents/*, carleson, Zeta3Irrational, leancert, PrimeCert) are never imported. Fixing these makes the machine-readable catalogue trustworthy; this study's own catalogue.json inherits the yaml gap.

title: Comparator: enforce or warn on definition holes whose challenge body is not sorry
summary: Comparator compares only name, type, universes and safety for definition_names targets, never bodies. In this repo, 8 of 10 hole configs show complete non-sorry bodies, e.g. all 12 Brenier OT definitions, which a reader would assume are enforced. A manual diff found no exploitation, but the guarantee as published is weaker than it looks. A mode that requires body equality when the challenge body is not sorry closes a silent-weakening channel for every AI-proof evaluation using Comparator.

targets.name: Brenier.json: 12 non-sorry defs listed as holes

beneficiaries: Lean FRO / AIMO-style evaluations, every lab publishing AI-generated Lean with Comparator configs
first_step: Open an issue/PR on leanprover/comparator: when a definition_names target's challenge value is not sorryAx-headed, compare values (or emit a warning), with an explicit opt-out flag.
measurement: PR merged; rerun on the 10 OAI hole configs flags exactly the non-sorry ones.
risks: Some legitimate challenges expect different bodies; needs a clear opt-out. Small user base outside AI-eval settings.

title: Close 266's headline N(6)=3: publish/rerun the binary64 execution archive, then kernel-check it via interval certificates
summary: Lean proves only N(6)<=5 (plus Fourier vanishing off Tao's class). The headline 'four MUBs impossible' is a 4,470 s binary64 branch-and-bound whose cited archive (verification/computation, REPRODUCE.md) is absent from the repo, although 30 other manuscripts ship verification/. Stage 1 (publish and rerun) is cheap. Stage 2 (Lean interval certificates over a 12^5-cell base cover) is a large, GB-scale project. Application value is modest, because the design-relevant 'no complete set of 7' is already formal.

targets.name: docs/266.md scope (does not establish the bound three)

first_step: Request the execution archive from OpenAI, or open an issue; rerun the 100-process pipeline on two different platforms and compare the published SHA-256 hashes.
measurement: Archive published and reproduced (stage 1); Lean statement 'Attainable n -> n <= 3' Comparator-checked (stage 2).
risks: The archive may not be releasable. A binary64 to interval translation may need re-engineering of the cover. The Lean artifact would be very large (<=5 alone is 2.8M lines/205 MB).

title: Upstream a finite reversible Markov chain API (spectral gap -> TV/mixing time, Dirichlet form, canonical paths) to Mathlib, seeded by 131
summary: Mathlib HEAD has measure-theoretic Kernel.IsReversible/Invariant but no MarkovChain, mixing time, spectral gap, Dirichlet form or TV distance. The OAI library re-defines mixingTime 15 times and TV 40 times. 131's generic layer (~800 lines, Mathlib-only imports: matrix_tv_bound_of_gap, energy algebra, spectral-from-square) is a good seed but assumes a symmetric kernel with uniform stationary law. It must be generalized to reversible pi and rewritten to Mathlib style.
beneficiaries: Formal verification of MCMC samplers (switch/Curveball, card shuffles, Glauber dynamics), Mathlib probability maintainers
first_step: Zulip RFC in #mathlib4 > probability proposing Matrix.IsReversible pi, spectralGap, tvDist and the gap-to-TV theorem, with 131's proof as the reference.
measurement: Merged PRs; 131's switch_chain_tv_bound re-proved on the Mathlib API.
risks: Design debates (finite matrices vs Kernel) can stall PRs. The code needs substantial rewriting (30,858 OAI files use bare 'import Mathlib', non-Mathlib style). Maintainer bandwidth.

title: Upstream circulant Hadamard (n in {1,4}) and even-Barker classification onto Mathlib's new Matrix.IsHadamard
summary: Mathlib added Matrix.IsHadamard in 2026 and has Matrix.circulant, so the classical theorem can be stated natively over R. OAI's proof is 68 files/9.5k lines with Mathlib-only imports (cyclotomic, 2-adic, Kronecker root-of-unity arguments), much of which probably overlaps existing Mathlib API. A small, self-contained, classic first upstream.
beneficiaries: Mathlib combinatorial-design users, formal-conjectures, sequence-design references
first_step: State Matrix.IsHadamard (circulant v) over R implies card n in {1,4} in Mathlib terms; port OAI's proof file by file, replacing local cyclotomic lemmas with Mathlib ones.
measurement: Merged Mathlib PR(s); line count after deduplication vs the 9.5k original.
risks: Licensing/attribution of AI-generated code in Mathlib (Apache-2.0 on both sides; norms still evolving); reviewer time.

title: Upstream numerical range + Toeplitz-Hausdorff convexity (from 325), then the Crouzeix 2-bound
summary: Mathlib has no numerical range. OAI proves its convexity four separate times (142-333 lines each). A few-hundred-line PR gives Mathlib W(A), compactness, convexity and the spectrum-in-closure lemma. The 15k-line complete-Crouzeix proof is a natural follow-up that formally underpins field-of-values bounds used in GMRES/Arnoldi analyses.
beneficiaries: Mathlib operator-theory users; numerical-linear-algebra formalization efforts
first_step: PR Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NumericalRange.lean with the definition for continuous linear maps plus Toeplitz-Hausdorff, ported from OAI HilbertCrouzeix/NumericalRange.lean.
measurement: Merged PR; Crouzeix bound stated against the Mathlib definition.
risks: Low; the main risk is reviewer bandwidth. The Crouzeix follow-up is heavy.

title: Specht modules / unitary S_n representations from 238 (YoungSymmetry + FiniteUnitary)
summary: Mathlib has YoungDiagram and SemistandardTableau but no Specht modules. OAI has 1.9k + 3.2k lines building unitary Specht representations for the Thorp analysis. This is a long-standing Mathlib gap, but the OAI code is purpose-built and needs redesign.
first_step: Zulip RFC comparing OAI's construction with planned Mathlib designs.
measurement: RFC outcome; any merged Specht definition.
risks: Design mismatch with Mathlib's Representation API; no applied pull.

title: Strict omega-categories, Street nerve, Kan-Quillen model structure from 317
summary: The 317 closure (65k live lines; 94.7k of Thomason's 160k lines are dead code) contains a full ModelCategory SSet (Kan-Quillen). Mathlib HEAD lacks this, but it duplicates Joel Riou's in-flight formalization, and the weak equivalences use a custom pi_n-bijection definition. OmegaCategory, Steiner complexes, orientals and the Street nerve are genuinely new to Lean, but have no applied users.

measurement: Whether any lemma or design is adopted.

title: DO NOT: 'formalize 003's quasi-RH top line'
summary: Already done. riemannZeta s != 0 and DirichletCharacter.LFunction chi s != 0 for 7/8 < Re s (every modulus and character, pole excluded) are Comparator targets stated purely with Mathlib objects, and Hecke over Q(sqrt-3) and the Siegel gap are also formal. The 11/12 alternate proof adds nothing. The Siegel constant is ineffective, so no formal explicit constant is available for CAS/explicit-PNT use. Effort belongs in lean-1 (replaying these four configs).

title: DO NOT: use the triage lean=true flag (or catalogue 'formalized') as the confidence column
summary: lean=true (242 families) overrates 14 families whose formalization is only supporting or weaker (incl. 266 N(6)=3, 195, 261, 194) and ~8 where a headline clause is omitted (095 no-lift, 149 permanence). Conversely, catalogue.json's per-manuscript 'formalized' flag comes from yaml sources only (172) and marks Comparator-backed 131/374/266/012/187/317 as unformalized. Use lean_confidence.json and each doc's scope paragraph instead.

title: DO NOT: build, vendor, or bulk-upstream the 26M-line OAI library
summary: The library is 1.57 GB of source (16x Mathlib) with 1.21M dead lines, 30,858 files using bare 'import Mathlib', machine-certificate bulk (Ramsey 223 MB, MUB 205 MB, 444k kernel decide calls), and 15 unused git dependencies. The README itself recommends compiling small portions. Verify per closure (lean-1) and upstream by extraction and rewrite (lean-6/7/8).

risks: Weeks of CI time and maintainer friction for no marginal assurance.

title: DO NOT: rely on or formalize explicit constants (Thorp round counts, 374 C*, 021 C, 149 eps) for applications
summary: The formal statements are existential or asymptotic: Thorp TV->0 'eventually in d' after 2048d shuffles (1600d only in the library), 32,800d from worst start, and (1/2)N^-5 after an unspecified sweep count. That is 51k-65k shuffles at N=2^32 versus a ~64 lower bound, so no fixed-N certificate for FPE. 374/021/149 assert 'exists C/eps'. Formalizing the papers' explicit constants (e.g. 374's C*~96) would certify bounds too loose for practice.
